revision.comment: 富木車塚古墳のページを作りました。
revision.text:
[[高石市]]に、かつてあった[[前方後円墳]]。
全国各地に点在する[[車塚古墳]]の１つ、である。
宅地造成工事のため破壊され、現在は、立札があるのみである。

{{sd|記事1|百科事典としての解説に足る定義がない}} [[高石市]]に、かつてあった[[前方後円墳]]。
全国各地に点在する[[車塚古墳]]の１つ、である。
宅地造成工事のため破壊され、現在は、立札があるのみである。

{{sd|記事1|百科事典としての解説に足る定義がない}} '''富木車塚古墳'''(とのきくるまづかこふん)は、[[大阪府]][[高石市]]にかつてあった[[前方後円墳]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isekiwalker.com/iseki/110615/|title=富木車塚古墳：遺跡ウォーカー|accessdate=2018-05-22}}</ref>。６世紀後半に作られ、近くの旧富木村付近の氏族の墓とみられる。
１９５９年、[[大阪市立美術館]]と[[高石町]]が共同で調査した。
全国各地に点在する[[車塚古墳]]の１つである。
宅地造成工事のため破壊され、現在は立札があるのみである。
== 大きさ == 全長４５メートル。最大高さ５メートル。
前方部は、幅１８メートル。最大高さ３.２メートル。
後円部は、直径２５メートル、最大高さ５メートル。
後円部に、全長７メートルの横穴式石室があったほか、墳丘上の６か所に埋葬木棺が出土し、少なくとも十数人分の人物が埋葬されていた。
== 出土品 == 豊富な装身具が、出土している。とくに女子用とみられる、金銀とガラス玉を併用した玉具が出土している。
また、首飾りも、変化に富んでいる。
== 交通アクセス == ＪＲ阪和線富木駅から、西へ徒歩１０分。

特徴的なのは、豊富な装身具の出土で、女子用とみられる金銀とガラス玉を併用した玉具や、首飾りがみられる。

revision.comment: 古墳が破壊された経緯について、追記しました。
revision.text:
{{sd|記事1|百科事典としての解説に足る定義がない}} '''富木車塚古墳'''(とのきくるまづかこふん)は、[[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石３丁目にかつてあった[[前方後円墳]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isekiwalker.com/iseki/110615/|title=富木車塚古墳：遺跡ウォーカー|accessdate=2018-05-22}}</ref>。６世紀後半に作られ、近くの旧[[取石村]]付近を根拠地とした古代氏族の殿来[[連]]との関連がいわれている。
１９５９年、[[大阪市立美術館]]と[[高石町]]が共同で調査した。
全国各地に点在する[[車塚古墳]]の１つ、である。
宅地造成工事のため破壊され、現在は立札があるのみである。
== 大きさ == 全長４５メートル。最大高さ５メートル。
前方部は、幅１８メートル。最大高さ３.２メートル。
後円部は、直径２５メートル、最大高さ５メートル。
後円部に、全長７メートルの珍しい右片袖型の横穴式石室があったほか、墳丘上の６か所に埋葬木棺が出土し、少なくとも十数人分の人物が埋葬されていた。
== 出土品 == 耳環・玉類・馬具・武具・鉄刀・鉄鉾・鉄鏃・石突・鉄釘などが、出土した<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.skao.net/yokoana/|title=横穴式石室研究会|accessdate=2018年5月22日|publisher=}}</ref>。
特徴的なのは、豊富な装身具の出土で、女子用とみられる金銀とガラス玉を併用した玉具や、首飾りがみられる。
== 交通アクセス == ＪＲ阪和線富木駅から、西へ徒歩１０分。
== 古墳破壊問題 == 戦後、大阪府下では、諸事情により多数の[[古墳]]が破壊された。全長１００メートルを超える古代史研究に少なからず影響を与えるような規模の古墳も、含まれている。
この古墳も、同様に1962年（昭和36年）4～5月ころに破壊された。この古墳と同じ、[[車塚古墳]]と呼ばれる全国各地のものの多くが[[国史跡]]に指定されていることから、非常に重大な文化破壊であった。宅地造成を急ぐあまり、学術調査を免罪符にした事情がある<ref>日本建築学会論文報告集第69号昭和36年10月斎藤和夫「市街地再開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」</ref>。

この古墳も、同様に1962年（昭和37年）4～5月ころに破壊された。この古墳と同じ[[車塚古墳]]と呼ばれる全国各地のものの多くが[[国史跡]]に指定され、そのなかには天皇の[[陵墓参考地]]になっているものもあることから、非常に重大な文化破壊であった。宅地造成を急ぐあまり、学術調査を免罪符にした事情がある<ref>日本建築学会論文報告集第69号昭和36年10月斎藤和夫「市街地再開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」</ref>。邪馬台国に関連があると思われる[[和泉黄金塚古墳]]に近接していたことも、注目される。
== 脚注 == {{reflist}}

{{sd|記事1|百科事典としての解説に足る定義がない}} '''富木車塚古墳'''(とのきくるまづかこふん)は、[[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石３丁目にかつてあった[[前方後円墳]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isekiwalker.com/iseki/110615/|title=富木車塚古墳：遺跡ウォーカー|accessdate=2018-05-22}}</ref>。６世紀後半に作られ、近くの旧[[取石村]]付近を根拠地とした古代氏族の殿来[[連]]との関連がいわれている。
１９５９年、[[大阪市立美術館]]と[[高石町]]が共同で調査した。
全国各地に点在する[[車塚古墳]]の１つ、である。
宅地造成工事のため破壊され、現在は立札があるのみである。
== 大きさ == 全長４５メートル。最大高さ５メートル。
前方部は、幅１８メートル。最大高さ３.２メートル。
後円部は、直径２５メートル、最大高さ５メートル。
後円部に、全長７メートルの珍しい右片袖型の横穴式石室があったほか、墳丘上の６か所に埋葬木棺が出土し、少なくとも十数人分の人物が埋葬されていた。
== 出土品 == 耳環・玉類・馬具・武具・鉄刀・鉄鉾・鉄鏃・石突・鉄釘などが、出土した<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.skao.net/yokoana/|title=横穴式石室研究会|accessdate=2018年5月22日|publisher=}}</ref>。
特徴的なのは、豊富な装身具の出土で、女子用とみられる金銀とガラス玉を併用した玉具や、首飾りがみられる。
== 交通アクセス == [[JR]][[阪和線]][[富木駅]]から、西へ徒歩１０分。
== 古墳破壊問題 == 戦後、大阪府下では、諸事情により多数の[[古墳]]が破壊された。全長１００メートルを超える古代史研究に少なからず影響を与えるような規模の古墳も、含まれている。
この古墳も、同様に1962年（昭和37年）4～5月ころに破壊された。この古墳と同じ[[車塚古墳]]と呼ばれる全国各地のものの多くが[[国史跡]]に指定され、そのなかには天皇の[[陵墓参考地]]になっているものもあることから、非常に重大な文化破壊であった。宅地造成を急ぐあまり、学術調査を免罪符にした事情がある<ref>日本建築学会論文報告集第69号昭和36年10月斎藤和夫「市街地再開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」</ref>。
[[邪馬台国]]に関連があると思われる[[和泉黄金塚古墳]]に近接していたことも、注目される。
== 脚注 == {{reflist}}

revision.text:
{{日本の古墳 |名称 = 富木車塚古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
富木車塚古墳跡 説明板 |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石3丁目 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 31|緯度秒 = 21.80 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 26|経度秒 = 52.27 |ISO = JP-27 |形状 = [[前方後円墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長48m
高さ5m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 7基（[[横穴式石室]]1基ほか） |出土品 = 副葬品多数 |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]中葉 |被葬者 = 11人 |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Osaka |アイコン = 前方後円墳-北西 |ラベル = 富木車塚
古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''富木車塚古墳'''（とのきくるまづかこふん）は、[[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。現在では墳丘は失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+和泉北部の首長墓系譜 !colspan=2|群!!古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期 |- |北|| ||[[和泉黄金塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||94m||4c末 |- | ||南||丸笠山古墳||前方後円墳||96m||4c末 |- | ||南||鍋塚古墳||[[円墳]]||60-70m||5c初 |- | ||南||王塚古墳||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||46m||5c中 |- |北|| ||信太貝吹山古墳||帆立貝形古墳||60m||5c前 |- |北|| ||カニヤ塚古墳||帆立貝形古墳||不明||5c後 |- |北|| ||大園古墳||帆立貝形古墳||50m||5c末 |- |北|| ||'''富木車塚古墳'''||前方後円墳||48m||6c中 |- | ||南||狐塚古墳||前方後円墳||58m||6c後 |}
大阪府南部、低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 構造 == 古墳の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 主体部の埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第1主体・第2主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=[[小林三郎 (考古学者)|小林三郎]]|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+和泉北部の首長墓系譜 !colspan=2|群!!古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期 |- |北|| ||[[和泉黄金塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||94m||4c末 |- | ||南||丸笠山古墳||前方後円墳||96m||4c末 |- | ||南||鍋塚古墳||[[円墳]]||60-70m||5c初 |- | ||南||王塚古墳||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||46m||5c中 |- |北|| ||[[信太貝吹山古墳]]||帆立貝形古墳||60m||5c前 |- |北|| ||カニヤ塚古墳||帆立貝形古墳||不明||5c後 |- |北|| ||[[大園古墳]]||帆立貝形古墳||50m||5c末 |- |北|| ||'''富木車塚古墳'''||前方後円墳||48m||6c中 |- | ||南||狐塚古墳||前方後円墳||58m||6c後 |}
大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 構造 == 古墳の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 主体部の埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第1主体・第2主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=[[小林三郎 (考古学者)|小林三郎]]|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}（学術調査済であることを口実として破壊された例の1つ斎藤和夫 「市街地開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」『日本建築学会論文報告集』第69号、日本建築学会、1961年。）。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 構造 == 古墳の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 主体部の埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第2主体・第3主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=[[小林三郎 (考古学者)|小林三郎]]|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}（学術調査済であることを口実として破壊された例の1つ斎藤和夫 「市街地開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」『日本建築学会論文報告集』第69号、日本建築学会、1961年。）。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。主体部の埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 主体部の埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第2主体・第3主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=小林三郎|authorlink=小林三郎 (考古学者)|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}（学術調査済であることを口実として破壊された例の1つ斎藤和夫 「市街地開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」『日本建築学会論文報告集』第69号、日本建築学会、1961年。）。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第2主体・第3主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=小林三郎|authorlink=小林三郎 (考古学者)|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Kohanezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} || {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 25 meters ** Height: 5 meters * Front Section ** Width: 18 meters ** Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Kohanezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ** Diameter: 25 meters ** Height: 5 meters * Front Section ** Width: 18 meters ** Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[category:original pages]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Togidensha Kofun]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:mass bump]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]]

No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational {{Infobox ancient site | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational {{Infobox ancient site | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
