Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue ware. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! Shape !! Size !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | Group !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Informational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | group = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial_chamber = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | artifacts = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | designation = Not designated }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated dimensions are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == Burial Facilities == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. Artifacts include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. Artifacts include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. Artifacts include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. Artifacts include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. Artifacts include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial.
