So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | size = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. {{afc comment|1=trimming these off. the parameter works as "burial" so no need to use "burial"[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:35, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=added parameters Interred_individual and Mausoleum is planned to be added but I messed up in template editing[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:40, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=now we have a 'burial' and 'burial goods' parameter. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | area = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! Period |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | area = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! built |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun (富木車塚古墳) | image = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | area = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! built |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | other_designation = Not other_designation1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! built |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | area = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | Historic Site = Not Historic Site1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | Historic Site = Not Historic Site1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Intypeational sign at the site of Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun | alternate_name = | part_of = | location = {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|34|31|21.80|N|135|26|52.27|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} | area = Mound length: 48m
Height: 5m (rear circular section) | burial = 7 burial facilities (including one {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}) | burial goods = Numerous burial goods | period = Mid [[6th century]] | Historic Site = Not Historic Site1 }} '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' (富木車塚古墳) was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} located in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ja|高石市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}, Japan. The mound is no longer extant. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Lineage of Izumi Northern Chief Tombs ! colspan="2" | part_of !! Tomb name !! type !! area !! built |- | North || || {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}}|| {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || 94m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Marukasa-yama Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 96m || Late 4th century |- | || South || Nabetsuka Kofun || {{ill|Empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 60–70m || Early 5th century |- | || South || Ōtsuka Kofun || {{ill|Hotategaigata Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} || 46m || Mid-5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Shinoda Kaibukiyama Kofun|ja|信太貝吹山古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 60m || Early 5th century |- | North || || Kaniya-zuka Kofun || Hotategaigata Kofun || Unknown || Late 5th century |- | North || || {{ill|Ōzono Kofun|ja|大園古墳}} || Hotategaigata Kofun || 50m || Late 5th century |- | North || || '''Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun''' || Zenpokoenfun || 48m || Mid-6th century |- | || South || Kitsunezuka Kofun || Zenpokoenfun || 58m || Late 6th century |}
Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:making categorization show up on newly imported categories and templates]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:completion tier 4]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:New2]] [[Category:pages which might possibly be incomplete but are most likely complete]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber
