Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}} [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]] {{draft categories| [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:completion tier 4]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] {{Kofun navbar}} {{Kofun navbar}}

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|ja|和泉黄金塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft|12=draft}} {{draft categories| }} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Takaishi, Osaka]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|12=draft|12=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|12=draft|12=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|12=draft|12=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|12=draft|12=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|12=draft|12=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|12=draft|12=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|qq=draft|qq=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 富木車塚古墳 |画像 = [[File:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun, setsumeiban.jpg|280px]]
富木車塚古墳跡 説明板 |別名 = |所属 = |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石3丁目 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 31|緯度秒 = 21.80 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 26|経度秒 = 52.27 |ISO = JP-27 |形状 = [[前方後円墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長48m
高さ5m（後円部） |埋葬施設 = 7基（[[横穴式石室]]1基ほか） |出土品 = 副葬品多数 |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]中葉 |被葬者 = 11人 |陵墓 = |史跡 = なし |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = 墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Osaka |アイコン = 前方後円墳-北西 |ラベル = 富木車塚
古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''富木車塚古墳'''（とのきくるまづかこふん）は、[[大阪府]][[高石市]]西取石にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。現在では墳丘は失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+和泉北部の首長墓系譜 !colspan=2|群!!古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期 |- |北|| ||[[和泉黄金塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||94m||4c末 |- | ||南||丸笠山古墳||前方後円墳||96m||4c末 |- | ||南||鍋塚古墳||[[円墳]]||60-70m||5c初 |- | ||南||王塚古墳||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||46m||5c中 |- |北|| ||[[信太貝吹山古墳]]||帆立貝形古墳||60m||5c前 |- |北|| ||カニヤ塚古墳||帆立貝形古墳||不明||5c後 |- |北|| ||[[大園古墳]]||帆立貝形古墳||50m||5c末 |- |北|| ||'''富木車塚古墳'''||前方後円墳||48m||6c中 |- | ||南||狐塚古墳||前方後円墳||58m||6c後 |}
大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}（学術調査済であることを口実として破壊された例の1つ斎藤和夫 「市街地開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」『日本建築学会論文報告集』第69号、日本建築学会、1961年。）。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第2主体・第3主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=小林三郎|authorlink=小林三郎 (考古学者)|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

大阪府南部、信太山丘陵北西麓の低位段丘の先端部に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。[[1959年]]（[[昭和]]34年）に発掘調査が実施されたのち、昭和40年代後半に宅地開発で消滅している{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}（学術調査済であることを口実として破壊された例の1つ斎藤和夫 「市街地開発に伴う古墳の壊滅問題」『日本建築学会論文報告集』第69号、日本建築学会、1961年。）。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を北西方に向けた{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められておらず、墳丘周囲に周濠も認められていない{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]1基を含む計7基で、合計11人が副葬品とともに埋葬される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。またくびれ部においても祭祀を反映した大量の[[須恵器]]群が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 この富木車塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃の築造と推定される。有力豪族の家族墓として当時の家族構成を知るうえで重要視される古墳で、被葬者は明らかでないが『[[続日本紀]]』などに見える殿来連（とのきのむらじ、殿来氏）との関連が指摘される（付近では[[等乃伎神社]]の鎮座も知られる）「高石市」『日本歴史地名大系 28 大阪府の地名』 平凡社、1986年。。和泉地方北部では首長墓古墳として北群・南群の2群が認められるが、北群・南群にはそれぞれ時期的空白が認められることから両群が輪番制で首長を担ったと推定され、本古墳はそのうちの1つに位置づけられる「和泉北部の首長系譜」『和泉市の考古・古代・中世 （和泉市の歴史6）』 和泉市史編さん委員会編、和泉市・ぎょうせい、2013年、pp. 65-70。『大園遺跡発掘調査報告書 -土地区画整理事業に伴う葛の葉地区の調査-』 和泉市教育委員会、2014年、pp. 1-4。。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り（数字は推定規模）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 * 墳丘長：48メートル * 後円部 ** 直径：25メートル ** 高さ：5メートル * 前方部 ** 幅：18メートル ** 高さ：3メートル 墳丘はすべて盛土によって構築される{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設は、後円部3基（埋葬6人）・前方部4基（埋葬5人）の計7基（埋葬11人）{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。内容は次の通り。 ; 後円部 : 各主体は前方部に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。第2主体・第3主体は墳丘築造途中で構築され、第1主体に先行する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - [[横穴式石室]]で、石室全長約7メートル・幅1.2メートルを測る。内部には陶棺・木棺が据えられ、金環・管玉・銀うつろ玉・直刀片・鉾などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - [[粘土槨]]で、長さ1.94メートル・幅0.8メートルを測る。直刀・石鏃・須恵器などが検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬で、長さ2.48メートル・幅0.55メートルを測る。直刀・埋木棗玉・首飾が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 ; 前方部 : 各主体は後円部に後続する{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第1主体 - 木棺直葬。鹿角製環頭大刀・鉄鏃・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第2主体 - 木棺直葬。埋葬は2名。鉄剣・玉類・金環が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第3主体 - 木棺直葬。鉄刀・金環・須恵器が検出されている{{Sfn|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}。 :* 第4主体 - 木棺直葬。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（高石市、1994年設置） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1986|chapter=富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 28 大阪府の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（平凡社）|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=小林三郎|authorlink=小林三郎 (考古学者)|year=1989|chapter=車塚古墳 > 富木車塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|富木車塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1960|chapter=|title=富木車塚古墳（大阪市立美術館学報III）|publisher=[[大阪市立美術館]]|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[和泉黄金塚古墳]] * [[等乃伎神社]] {{デフォルトソート:とのきくるまつかこふん}} [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]] [[Category:前方後円墳]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|qq=draft|qq=draft}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukiishi|qq=}} or {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniwa|qq=}} were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}}, were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[6th century]] during the late {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}}."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumi City History Volume 6|qq=}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉市の歴史6|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumi City History Volume 6|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki no Muraji clan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, mentioned in the [[:en:Shoku Nihongi|Shoku Nihongi]], as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * [[:en:Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun]] * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|富木車塚古墳|version=93995667|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:高石市の歴史]]

The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki no Muraji clan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, mentioned in the [[:en:Shoku Nihongi|Shoku Nihongi]], as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki no Muraji clan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, mentioned in the [[:en:Shoku Nihongi|Shoku Nihongi]], as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * [[:en:Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun]] * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|富木車塚古墳|version=93995667|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Takaishi]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. The tumulus is believed to have been constructed in the mid-[[:en:6th century|6th century]] during the late [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]]."Lineage of Izumi Northern Chiefs," in {{ill|Izumi City History Volume 6|ja|和泉の Municipal History6|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumi City History Volume 6|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}: Archaeology, Ancient, and Medieval, Izumi City Editorial Committee, Izumi City, Gyosei, 2013, pp. 65–70. It is considered significant for understanding family structures among powerful clans in the region at the time. The tomb has been linked to the {{ill|Tonoki no Muraji clan|ja|殿来氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki no Muraji clan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, mentioned in the [[:en:Shoku Nihongi|Shoku Nihongi]], as well as to the nearby {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}}."Takaishi City," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. == Mound Specifications == The mound's estimated area are as follows: * Mound Length: 48 meters * Rear Circular Section ''' Diameter: 25 meters ''' Height: 5 meters * Front Section ''' Width: 18 meters ''' Height: 3 meters The mound was constructed entirely of piled earth. == burial == The burial facilities included seven separate chambers—three in the rear circular section (six individuals) and four in the front section (five individuals). Details are as follows: ; Rear Circular Section : These burials predate those in the front section. :* Chamber 1: {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, approximately 7m long and 1.2m wide, containing ceramic and wooden coffins. burial goods include gold rings, tubular beads, hollow silver beads, fragments of swords, and spears. :* Chamber 2: Clay coffin, measuring 1.94m by 0.8m. burial goods include iron swords, stone arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial, measuring 2.48m by 0.55m. burial goods include swords, wooden beads, and necklaces. ; Front Section : These burials occurred after those in the rear section. :* Chamber 1: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include antler hilt swords, iron arrowheads, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 2: Direct wooden coffin burial. Two individuals were interred. burial goods include iron swords, beads, and gold rings. :* Chamber 3: Direct wooden coffin burial. burial goods include swords, gold rings, and Sue pottery. :* Chamber 4: Direct wooden coffin burial. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == {{small|(Sources used for this article)}} * Intypeational sign (Takaishi City, 1994) * {{Cite book|language=ja|year=1986|chapter=Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=458249028X|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Heibonsha)|1986}}}} * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Kobayashi, Saburō|year=1989|chapter=Kurumazuka Kofun > Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun|title={{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}|publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Tonoki Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}}} == Related Articles == * [[:en:Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun]] * {{ill|Tonoki Shrine|ja|等乃伎神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tonoki Shrine|qq=}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|富木車塚古墳|version=93995667|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[ja:富木車塚古墳]] [[sn:onoki Kurumazuka Kofun]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal History of Takaishi]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] [[Category:qq]][[en:Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]]

Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. The tumulus was a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] with the front section oriented northwest.Kobayashi, Saburō. "Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|ja|日本古墳大辞典|1=Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Comprehensive Dictionary of Japanese Kofun|qq=}}, Tokyo-do Publishing, 1989. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. The burial facilities included seven chambers containing the remains of 11 individuals along with various grave goods. Ritual ceramics, including large quantities of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]], were also recovered from the mound's neck section. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. The site was excavated in 1959, but the mound was destroyed in the late 1960s due to residential development."Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun," in {{ill|Japanese Historical Topography Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Historical Topography Series|qq=}} Osaka Volume, Heibonsha, 1986. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961. No [[:en:Fukiishi|Fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]] were found on the mound, and there was no evidence of a surrounding moat. Tonoki Kurumazuka Kofun was located on the northwestern terrace of the {{ill|Shinodayama Hills|ja|信太山丘陵|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinodayama Hills|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 信太山演習場}} in southern Osaka. This destruction occurred despite the site having been archaeologically surveyed.Saitō, Kazuo. "The Problem of Kofun Destruction Due to Urban Development," in {{ill|Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja|日本建築学会論文報告集|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Journal of Architectural Institute of Japan|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Vol. 69, Architectural Institute of Japan, 1961.
